q1.answer_given: The peak-traffic cascade drove the decision to put a message queue in front of the enrichment step.

q2.answer_given: Because the handler waited synchronously, a slow call held the sender's connection open for that same duration, which then ran long enough to exceed the sender's timeout.

q3.answer_given: Each retry was itself a new synchronous call to the same slow endpoint, so retries added pressure instead of relieving it.

q4.answer_given: No — the loop stayed small enough to go unnoticed during ordinary traffic; it only ran hot enough to cascade during peak traffic.

q5.answer_given: No — receiver latency no longer depends on enrichment latency (decoupled), so a slow downstream call no longer produces a sender-facing timeout.

q6.answer_given: Fully eliminated — 'the specific retry-storm failure mode that caused the cascades is gone entirely, not just less frequent.'

q7.answer_given: A worker process handles enrichment work instead of it being done inline.

q8.answer_given: Acknowledgement happens first, immediately on receipt, instead of waiting on enrichment; hand-off to the worker happens after.

q1.answer_given: The peak-traffic cascade drove the decision to queue enrichment instead of calling it inline.

q2.answer_given: The handler called the enrichment API directly and held the connection open until it returned (Handler behavior), and the API was already slow (Downstream API); this is listed as producing 'connection held open' then 'sender timeouts' as direct effects.

q3.answer_given: Retries added load (item IV under Direct effects), but no explicit reason is given for why they add rather than relieve pressure.

q4.answer_given: No — the loop stays small enough to go unnoticed during ordinary traffic; it only cascades during peak traffic.

q5.answer_given: No — a slow call no longer produces a sender-facing timeout, because receiver latency is decoupled from enrichment latency.

q6.answer_given: The retry-storm failure mode is gone entirely, not just reduced.

q7.answer_given: A worker process, per the 'hand off to worker' step in the new flow.

q8.answer_given: Acknowledge immediately is step I, hand off to worker is step II, so acknowledgement happens first.
